headline: Wall Street ends its best week in more than a year with chips in the lead, but Treasuries sold off and the dollar firmed, so Friday's rally was about risk appetite rather than easier money

findings.headline: Stocks and bonds parted ways into the close
findings.body: The AP reports the S&P 500 closed out its best week in more than a year, with semiconductors leading the rebound from last week's AI-led rout. Bonds did not join in: the Treasury's par curve shows the 10-year yield at 4.94% on 27 November against 4.85% on 25 November, and the 2-year at 4.69% against 4.61%. CNBC ties the bond selloff to accelerating October inflation and next Friday's November payrolls, which feed straight into the December hike debate. Equities rising against higher real borrowing costs is the tension to watch next week, since a firm payrolls print would test the rebound.

findings.headline: The metals rally held even as the dollar turned higher
findings.body: This afternoon's rebound in precious metals was partly put down to a softer dollar, but by the close the dollar index was up on the day and US yields were higher, and silver, platinum and palladium still closed well up on the day, outpacing gold. That points to short covering and the broader return of risk appetite after this month's liquidation rather than a change in the rate outlook (analysis). The same rates backdrop that capped gold earlier in November is still in place.

findings.headline: Brent keeps its Gulf premium into Sunday's OPEC+ meeting while gas falls on weather
findings.body: Brent settled at $95.44 for January, ending a three-week losing streak, while WTI slipped 0.7% to $83.08 for a fourth weekly loss, so the widening gap between the two is the seaborne Gulf risk being priced. Kpler data cited by MarketWatch puts Hormuz flows at only 31% of prewar levels, and the Jazan refinery attack and an Iranian drone strike in Kuwait added to it. Sunday's OPEC+ meeting sets 2027 quotas from capacity assessments the Iran war has made hard to pin down. Gas moved the other way on both sides of the Atlantic: Henry Hub fell 4.6% to $3.491 on milder US forecasts after the Thanksgiving storm, and TTF also closed lower.

view: Our view: A strong week for risk assets has been built against rising yields, not falling ones, so next week's payrolls and Sunday's OPEC+ outcome matter more than the momentum; the metals bounce looks like positioning until the rates outlook softens.
